title: What the ECB tells markets when it does not publish a rate path
summary: Philip Lane describes a practical choice facing the ECB. Staff evaluate several plausible rate paths for every meeting, yet the collective public statement concentrates on the decision taken and the criteria for subsequent decisions. The staff projection uses the market curve as an assumption. It is neither the Council's forecast of its own rates nor an endorsement of market pricing. Lane notes the difficulty of agreeing conditional paths among 27 Council members and the danger that audiences may remember the path more readily than its conditions.

The publication sequence explains when the market can learn each part. In a typical cycle the 14:15 decision release precedes the 14:45 statement and questions. In projection rounds the detailed report follows at 15:45. The Economic Bulletin appears around two weeks later and the meeting account around four weeks later. The account reports presentations, policy options and discussion. Slide 6, drawing on January 2004 to October 2023, sums absolute movements around different communication events. The two-year overnight indexed swap moved more cumulatively around policy meetings than around presidential speeches, but speeches also contributed a large cumulative total. Event frequency and the length of each observation window affect these totals. Upward and downward changes across events both add to the total, so it measures movement without establishing direction or persistence.

Under the decision framework set out from March 2023, the Council considers the inflation outlook, underlying inflation and the strength of monetary transmission. Its 2025 update explicitly added surrounding risks. Energy and exchange-rate sensitivities help staff assess changes in assumptions. Public scenarios have focused on identifiable risks such as war, tariffs and the pandemic. A scenario can explain why today's decision reflects an unusual risk without assigning a probability or a policy rate to every future outcome. Publishing model-optimal alternative paths would add assumptions about both the model and policymakers' preferences.

The market evidence points to a difference between giving investors a path and giving them criteria with which to revise one. On slide 10 the estimated two-year swap response to a one-standard-deviation euro area data surprise is close to one tenth of a basis point under forward guidance. It is around 1.1 basis points in the period after directional guidance was withdrawn and roughly 0.8 in the subsequent reaction-function regime. The staff regression uses first differences in daily swap rates during 2007–26. News is measured against median forecasts for 59 indicators, scaled to each indicator's historical forecast errors and weighted by the fraction of Bloomberg users following it. The weights do not depend on the rate move. Correlated releases are adjusted to reduce double counting. The plotted 95% intervals are especially wide for the withdrawal period. Differences in shocks and macroeconomic conditions across regimes limit a causal comparison.

Language and pricing also measure different things. Staff score monetary policy, activity and inflation language separately. The history displayed on slide 11 smooths the last 30 texts. In a separate meeting-level regression, inflation language accounts for about four fifths of the combined standardised weight over the full sample. The weights on inflation and activity are constrained to sum to one. Inflation still receives the larger weight from July 2022. That ratio describes associations among words, not how many basis points the Council moves for an inflation surprise. Slide 12 decomposes selected meetings' multi-asset price movements into target, path and risk factors. An option-implied measure of uncertainty about three-month Euribor a year ahead is plotted on a different scale. A meeting can change the expected rate and uncertainty by different amounts.

Lane also shows where communication does not readily travel. In the August 2026 consumer survey nearly half reported no ECB information over the preceding two months. Television and radio reached roughly one third, comfortably ahead of the ECB's own website or social accounts. Respondents could report several channels. Counts of news articles and mentions of inflation on corporate earnings calls rose in the inflation surge, yet those series measure attention, not confidence in the ECB or a shift in expectations caused by a given speech.

The final slide estimates effects on industrial production and consumer prices using local projections for 2002–25. Staff remove monetary-policy tone predictable from inflation and activity language and communication between meetings. They then retain tone changes that move inversely with equities around the announcement. Both the communication shock and the policy-rate shock are scaled to raise the three-month swap rate by 25 basis points at its peak. The estimates show how an identified communication tightening can extend beyond financial markets, with a later decline in the price-level response. The paths fluctuate and the shaded bands are 68% intervals. These are conditional estimates for shocks meeting the authors' restrictions. An unadjusted hawkish sentence, or every policy meeting, does not meet that definition.

questions.question: Does reaction-function guidance improve pricing of genuinely new macroeconomic data?
questions.detail: Re-estimate slide 10 on indicators observed in every regime, separating inflation, activity and lending releases. Compare the front end with the ten-year rate when the component weights and news scaling are fixed in advance. Check changes in daily sensitivities against short announcement windows, particularly in the short post-withdrawal period where the reported intervals are wide.

questions.question: Can a communication shock identified from equities predict an instrument outside its construction?
questions.detail: Estimate the tone residual using only language available at the release, then distinguish the decision from the subsequent answers. Test pricing in unused maturities or contracts. Compare outcomes with and without the inverse-equity restriction and with the target-rate shock held comparable. This would show how much of the measured result requires the joint sign that selected those observations.

questions.question: Who actually changes inflation expectations after receiving ECB information?
questions.detail: Match the timing and channel of household exposure to revisions in one-year expectations, comparing people who previously reported similar beliefs and attention. Separate hearing about the ECB through broadcast coverage from seeking the central bank's material directly. The cross-sectional shares on slide 13 establish reach. An expectations response or a gain in credibility requires an additional comparison.
